subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw extend the Control UI agent file browser beyond the current read-only workspace API to support workspace editing and any system filesystem scope?
rationale: Current main intentionally split safe read-only workspace browsing from mutations, while this issue asks to widen read/write and possibly host filesystem access through a user-facing browser.

options.title: Keep Read-Only Now, Track CRUD Separately
options.body: Keep the current read-only workspace API as the safe landed slice and continue full workspace CRUD design in the canonical workspace-management thread.

options.title: Approve Workspace Editing Scope
options.body: Allow a rebased Control UI/Gateway implementation to add workspace-confined editing and destructive operations with explicit scopes, limits, audit posture, and proof.

options.title: Approve System Scope Design
options.body: Open a separate security design for host filesystem browsing because it is broader than agent workspace management and should not ride along with this issue.

recommendation.title: Keep Read-Only Now, Track CRUD Separately
recommendation.body: Keep the current read-only workspace API as the safe landed slice and continue full workspace CRUD design in the canonical workspace-management thread.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the landed read-only workspace API and related app surfaces, making them the clearest owner for the split between safe read-only access and broader filesystem capability.
